notes: First real execution found one kernel bug the harness exposed: raising the drift refusal INSIDE the decision write_txn rolled the invalidation back with it (status reverted to pending while the error claimed invalidated). Fixed by collecting refusals and raising AFTER commit, so the invalidation + its exactly-one event persist while the decision is refused; re-run all green.

Test-design lessons from the same first run: dedup tests must pin ONE subject (a fresh task per request is a different subject by task_id-in-fingerprint design); same-kind needs_input re-blocks legitimately route to triage at BLOCK_RECURRENCE_LIMIT, so re-bind scenarios use untyped blocks; the kanban_show approval hint is a projection of the block and disappears when approve releases the task.

unblock_task refactored into unblock_task + _unblock_task_in_txn (body unchanged, no own txn) so approve releases bound tasks inside the decision transaction with IDENTICAL semantics (parent re-gating, resume status, sticky-block exit) — proven by the untouched blocked_sticky/block_kinds/review suites.
Dispatcher untouched: no tick-path change, flags-off neutrality trivially preserved (approvals are queried only by CLI/tool surfaces, never by the tick).
